title: Concise inference architect briefing v1
content:
Purpose:
- One-page briefing for SEs/architects: 2–3 minute pitch to get buy-in from platform/infra/ML infra teams during discovery or technical kickoff. Not a full deck — minimal slides + rapid Q&A script.

Core positioning (two-line):
- Redwood Inference gives predictable LLM serving economics and SLOs across hosted, dedicated, and private deployment modes so platform teams avoid building and maintaining bespoke inference stacks.

Key buyer personas to address quickly:
- Platform/Infra Architect: cares about multi-tenant isolation, autoscaling, and SLA enforcement.
- ML Engineering Lead: cares about model fidelity, rollback, and quantization tradeoffs.
- Security/Compliance Engineer: needs VPC, KMS/HSM, auditability.

Opening 30s script (starter):
- "We help platform teams standardize LLM inference with a runtime that nails latency and cost while giving you policy-driven routing and guaranteed fallbacks. Two quick examples: (1) reduce per-token cost 30% via KV caching+batching without adding tail latency, (2) failover to quantized variants automatically when capacity spikes — customers keep SLAs without manual shims."

Rapid discovery questions (pick 3–4):
- What are your current p50 / p95 inference latencies for critical endpoints?
- Do you have peak burst patterns (time-of-day / campaign-driven) and how do you currently absorb them?
- Have you benchmarked quantized model variants for quality drops? Who owns regression monitoring?
- Are there regulatory or data residency constraints that require private deployments or dedicated capacity?

Pain -> Redwood value snippets (quick ref):
- Pain: unpredictable burst costs. Pitch: reserved capacity + autoscale policies + cost-by-route visibility.
- Pain: slow failovers when models/regions are down. Pitch: smart routing + model variant fallbacks + canary rollouts.
- Pain: ops heavy integration for KV caching. Pitch: built-in prefix/KV caching with workload-aware suggestions via Redwood Optimize.

Objections and canned responses:
- "We can't tolerate any quality regression from quantization." -> "We can run your eval suite against quantized candidates in our onboarding sandbox and surface token-level deltas; canary traffic routing keeps production on golden model until you accept the metric thresholds."
- "We already have autoscaling on our cluster." -> "Autoscaling is part of the solution, but routing + fallback policies and model-variant rollback reduce noisy-threshold failures and costly overprovisioning — think of us as the control plane for inference serving economics."
- "Vendor lock-in concerns." -> "Redwood exposes standard REST/SDKs and model pinning semantics; you retain control of model artifacts and can migrate preserved model builds. Private deployment option runs with your control plane."

Demo checklist for a 12–15 minute flow (SE sprint):
- 0:00–1:00 Intro + persona alignment.
- 1:00–3:00 Show latency/cost dashboard: token breakdown, per-route p50/p95, cost heatmap. (Highlight sample customer: ml-retailer reduced p95 by 18% with caching.)
- 3:00–6:00 Live routing policy demo: create a simple rule to prefer cheaper 8-bit variant for background tasks and gold model for user-facing flows. Show traffic split/rollout.
- 6:00–9:00 Canary + rollback: push a quantized build, run canary at 5% with SLA guard rails, simulate quality regression and auto-rollback.
- 9:00–12:00 Private deployment sketch: show VPC diagram, KMS integration, and audit log sample.
- 12:00–15:00 Q&A + next steps (POC invite, sandbox access).

Technical quick facts (to memorize):
- Typical caching gains: 20–40% token reduction on multi-turn chat flows (depends on repetition/prefix).
- Quantization profiles supported: 8-bit, 4-bit (experimental), with QC metrics surfaced per-token.
- Runtime optimizations: attention fusion, dynamic batching, KV cache hot-path — these shave 10–40% off per-token compute on standard LLM architectures.
- Metrics: present p50, p95, throughput (tokens/sec), cost-per-token; show sample of per-token CPU/GPU breakdown.

Canary & fallback shorthand (two-sentence):
- Create a rollout policy: percentage, time window, permissible quality delta. If quality delta > threshold or latency > SLO, route to fallback (compatible model variant or region). Fallbacks are first-class and chainable.

Pricing talking points (short):
- Hosted: usage (tokens) + premium for streaming/function call features; free tier credits for sandboxing.
- Dedicated: commit for predictable throughput; discounts scale with term.
- Private: license + setup fees for on-prem/VPC, enterprise support optional.
- Negotiation cue: buyers care about unit economics at 1M tokens/day — offer to run a quick cost comparison vs current infra during POC.

POC / pilot template (what to propose):
- 4 weeks, success criteria: maintain <= target p95 latency and < accepted quality delta vs golden model on evaluation set; demonstrate 20% cost improvement or clear operational simplicity win (fewer runbook steps).
- Deliverables: sandbox ingress, sample workload, dashboard access, weekly checkpoints, final recommendation doc.

Open issues / TODOs (notes to self):
- Pin a recent customer anonymized metric example for caching numbers (ask analytics for permission).
- Draft a 1-slide legal blurb for private deployments on data residency.
- Add a short script for finance asks (show ARR/commit examples).

Concise slide outline (3–6 slides):
1) Title + one-line pitch + 30s script.
2) Pain/Value bullets tailored to platform engineers.
3) Live demo checklist and success metrics.
4) Canary + fallback flow visual + negotiating cues.
5) POC template + next steps.
6) Appendix: quick facts + links to eval harness and Confluence runbooks.

Appendix links / references (internal):
- Confluence sandbox onboarding: CONFLUENCE-1234
- Eval harness + seed prompts repo: github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness
- Example ticket for private deploy checklist: JIRA-9987

Quick talk-track reminders (bullet form):
- Use concrete numbers when possible (p95 latency, % cost saving).
- When asked about model regression, pivot to "we run your eval suite + token-level diff" and offer to run a blind A/B.
- Avoid committing to exact savings — offer to run a side-by-side during POC.

End: this is intentionally short — aim to give SEs/AE a fast-to-memorize briefing for discovery calls and architect-level demos. Treat as living doc; update after three pilot runs with new anonymized metrics.
